originalTitle: Nepal flash flood live updates: more than 500 missing in Tibet, reports China, amid search for hundreds of tourists
summary: At least 165 people have died, while officials believe 340 foreign nationals from India, the US, UK, Australia, Malaysia and Ukraine among those missing. Follow the latest news
content: The US government expressed its condolences and promised to provide $500,000 in emergency assistance to Nepal, the state department said. The United States extends its deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of those who lost their lives in the devastating flash floods in the Rasuwa district of Nepal.” In a message on X, secretary of state Marco Rubio added his support, saying, “We express our solidarity and are united in prayer for the Nepali people following the devastating floods.” Eyewitness accounts have been emerging from the Tibetan side of the border, with a woman saying she was travelling from Gyirong town towards Nepal on Wednesday morning when her group encountered the flood about 4km from Gyirong port. “Trees and electricity poles had already been knocked down, and the flood water was bearing down on us. We didn’t dare turn around, so we could only reverse,” the woman, surnamed Fang, told Xiaoxiang Morning News. She eventually returned safely to Gyirong town but said that about 5pm was still unable to reach a friend who had been at the port. Separately, the husband of a worker on a Chinese road-rehabilitation project in Nepal said his wife had been staying at a project camp beside the river, about 3km from the Gyirong customs building. “We were still in contact last night. It wasn’t until 11am that I learned there had been a mudslide, and since then I haven’t been able to reach my wife or anyone at the project site,” he told China Newsweek. The project had three riverside camps employing about 60 Chinese workers, all of which had lost contact, he said. On the Nepal side of the border, a tourist said they suddenly heard “a roaring sound, as if the mountainside was being torn apart” before a torrent of mud surged through the valley. They said that at its closest the mud was only about a metre below where they were standing, telling Red Star News: I was really scared. My whole body was trembling. Continued from the last post on the number of people missing in Nepal: Japan Prime minister Sanae Takaichi said she was “concerned” by media reports that five Japanese nationals were missing after the flooding. South Africa Four South Africans travelling with the same Alpine Eco Trek agency as the British citizens were missing, according to the Nepal tourism board. United States Three US citizens, also with Fishtail Tours + Travels, were unaccounted for, the board said. Portugal Portugal’s foreign ministry said a woman and a man had gone missing in the floods. Netherlands A Dutch citizen travelling with the same company as the missing Australian was also unaccounted for, the board said. Italy The Italian foreign ministry said two of its nationals and their guide were stranded upstream from a landslide but were receiving help. The ministry was aware of 90 Italian citizens currently in Nepal and Tibet, but did not know if any might have been affected. Nationalities unconfirmed Several of the tour groups also announced missing foreigners whose nationalities had not been confirmed. They included 77 with Trekkers Society, 26 with Kailash Journey and eight with Richa Tours + Travels. Nepal The Nepali tourism board also said that, in addition to the unaccounted-for foreigners, a total of 93 Nepalis were missing. Hundreds of foreign nationals are missing in Nepal after the catastrophic flash flooding killed at least 160 people. Hikers and climbers from worldwide travel to the Himalayan nation to test themselves on some of the world’s highest peaks, Mount Everest among them. Here’s the latest on how many people are still out of contact in Nepal, care of Agence France-Presse. Chinese ‌state media has said separately that in Tibet’s Gyirong ⁠county the number of missing had risen to 558, including 260 foreign nationals. India According to the Nepal tourism board, 142 nationals from neighbouring India were missing. They were in the country with three travel agencies: Samrat Tours + Travels, Leaf Holiday and Himalayan Glacier. Ukraine Ukraine’s foreign ministry said Nepal’s tourist police had informed them that they believed 53 Ukrainian nationals were missing. They included a group of 46 Ukrainian tourists with whom the authorities in Nepal had lost contact, the ministry added. Malaysia Seventeen Malaysians travelling with Fishtail Tours + Travels were missing in the floods, the Nepal tourism board said. Malaysia’s foreign ministry said its embassy in Kathmandu had received reports from travel agencies suggesting they had lost contact with 11 Malaysian nationals believed to be in the Rasuwa district. Australia Thirty-four Australians are missing following the floods, prime minister Anthony Albanese said. UK Twelve UK citizens with the Alpine Eco Trek agency were unaccounted for, the tourism board said. South Korea The South Korean foreign ministry said nine hydropower workers were out of contact in the Rasuwa district. Continued next post The number of ⁠people ⁠missing in Tibet’s Gyirong ⁠county has ‌increased ‌to 558, according to Chinese state media, while Nepal says 468 tourists and travellers remain out of contact – putting the apparent overall number of missing at more than 1,000. Chinese ‌state broadcaster CCTV said on Thursday that of the 558 missing, 260 were foreign nationals, CCTV said. ⁠The death toll remained at three, it said. Separately, Nepal said 468 tourists and travellers – including 393 foreigners – remained out of contact on Thursday, 24 hours after the deadly flood tore through the border region with Tibet. It was not immediately certain the numbers of missing were entirely separate or if any had been counted twice in the two countries’ tallies. A Nepal tourism department spokesperson, Suraj Ghimire, told Agence France-Presse: “About 468 tourists and travellers are out of contact, among them 75 are Nepalis.” Here are some of the latest images coming in from the Nepal-Tibet border area as the disaster continues to unfold.
